context: a letter from John Lubbock, which you are answering
exchanges:
My brother in law Robert Birkbeck is going to spend some months in Corsica, & he thinks that Murray might possibly like some notes with reference to a Handbook for the Island.

He is anxious therefore for a note of introduction to him & I thought I might take the liberty of asking you to give him one.

If you would not mind adding, on my authority, that he is a man who will take pains to get accurate information, & whose statements would I think be thoroughly reliable, I should be very much obliged.

Hoping you are better again | I remain, dear Mr. Darwin, | Very sincerely yours | John Lubbock

C. Darwin Esq

I have embodied what you say, in the enclosed note of introduction to Mr Murray & I very sincerely hope it may answer its purpose.

We take this opportunity of returning with many thanks the beautiful book & the curious revolving machine which Lady Lubbock was so kind as to lend us.

I was so very sorry not to see you the other day when you called & hear about some wonderful new animal. You must have a knack of creating new animals down there.

yours very truly | Ch. Darwin
